liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (1 review): The reviewer says it swings strongly [4]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): The Cryptical Envelopment reprise segues into it, which the reviewer likes, as on 2/28/69 [6]
- **The Eleven** (1 review): Catches fire after China Cat Sunflower but ends too soon for the reviewer [9]
- **Born Cross-Eyed** (1 other source): Only the first couple of seconds of the song are missing from the tape [3]
- **Spanish Jam** (1 review): The reviewer says it really stands out [14]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): The band is screaming through it [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **Born Cross-Eyed**: rare: 14 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd68-03-30.aud.cotsman.14912.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 14 songs; 87 min; rated 4.16/5 by 19 [1]. Said about its sound: Tape is many generations removed from the source, with poor sound quality; The sound is a little murky, but it is listenable with equalizer adjustment; Sound is surprisingly clear for a 1968 audience tape [4][5][6][9][11][15]
- **gd1968-03-30.aud.unknown.9375.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 9 songs; 59 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [3]
- **gd1968-03-30.sbd.miller.108994.flac16**: soundboard; 9 songs; 67 min; rated 2.78/5 by 9 [2]

## Around the show

- Before the encore, Jerry has everyone shout out suggestions at the same time [15]
- Reviewer rates the live dates behind Anthem, including this one, as the band's peak [5]
- Good for a 1968 audience tape, but the Shrine 8/23 recording is better [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd68-03-30.aud.cotsman.14912.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Andy Lemieux and J Cotsman; source: Audience [1]. Also: Late March 1968 tapes are often labeled soundboards, but this one sounds like it was recorded by microphones on stage; Material on the second disc likely comes from a different show, though it circulates under the 3/30/68 date; Deadlists reportedly gives an unknown date for everything after the first Lovelight [1][4][6][14][15]
- **gd1968-03-30.aud.unknown.9375.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD>MR>D>PCM>D>CD [3]. Also: Well-made audience recording often mistaken for a soundboard; a large dropout early in Lovelight was reduced with Sound Forge; The second Lovelight, Beat It On Down The Line and Dancing In The Streets probably come from a different show [3]
- **gd1968-03-30.sbd.miller.108994.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> (4 Track) Master Reels -> Dat (44.1k) [2]
